title: Potain launches new heavyweight MDT 1609 and delivers first model to Germany
summary: The new crane is the largest in the Potain range of topless cranes, with a 40 t maximum capacity and the ability to lift 14.1 t at the end of its 80 m jib.German building materials and construction giant BACHL Group has received the first crane.Manitowoc Lift Solutions provided design and engineering support so the crane could be installed on an existing mast at the customer’s facility.
body_markdown:
## Seamless set-up on site


The Potain MDT 1609 was installed at the Karl Bachl Betonwerke facility on an existing circular mast of the previous tower crane on site. To manage this integration and installation, long-standing Potain dealer Moser Baumaschinen and Manitowoc’s specialized[Lift Solutions](https://www.manitowoc.com/sites/default/files/media/divers/file/2020-04/LiftSolutionsPotain-Brochure-EN.pdf) team developed a special adapter to seamlessly connect the upperworks of the MDT 1609 with the existing mast. The 3.2 m-diameter adapter measures 1.55 m tall and weighs 7.5 t.


“Each project for Lift Solutions is unique because we are tailoring engineered solutions specifically to the project. For the MDT 1609, we required all our engineering know-how and close cooperation with Moser Baumaschinen, with whom we’ve worked for over 30 years as a Potain dealer. The result was a huge success. The Potain MDT 1609 is the first in an exciting new line of Maxi-MDT cranes – high-performance topless cranes with the latest technology to tackle some of the most challenging applications,” said Bernard Ecabert, Lift Solutions manager for tower cranes at Manitowoc.


Karl Bachl Betonwerke is part of the[BACHL Group](https://www.bachl.de/) , one of Europe’s leading names in the construction and building materials segment, with 2,600 employees across production and sales sites in Germany, Austria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Italy, Poland, Romania, and Croatia. The company was founded in 1926 and produces a range of building materials, while its construction division handles projects from industrial and commercial construction to road building.
